title: Selective Context Slice Subscription
concept: Avoiding Full Re-renders with Slice Selectors
problemStatement: Implement `createSelectiveContextStore(initialState)` that allows consumers to subscribe only to a selected slice of context. Consumers are notified ONLY when their selected slice changes.
interviewTrap: Standard React Context cannot bail out of renders for partial state changes. Custom selector stores solve this problem.

testCases.name: Notifies slice subscriber when its slice changes
testCases.testFn: const store = createSelectiveContextStore({ user: 'Alice', theme: 'dark' }); const log = []; store.subscribeSlice(s => s.user, u => log.push(u)); store.setState({ user: 'Bob' }); return log;

testCases.name: Ignores updates to unrelated state slices
testCases.input: update theme does not notify user subscriber
testCases.testFn: const store = createSelectiveContextStore({ user: 'Alice', theme: 'dark' }); let calls = 0; store.subscribeSlice(s => s.user, () => calls++); store.setState({ theme: 'light' }); return calls;

testCases.name: Unsubscribe cleans up subscriber properly
testCases.testFn: const store = createSelectiveContextStore({ count: 0 }); let count = 0; const unsub = store.subscribeSlice(s => s.count, () => count++); store.setState({ count: 1 }); unsub(); store.setState({ count: 2 }); return count;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: When a Context Provider's `value` prop changes identity, EVERY component that calls `useContext(MyContext)` MUST re-render, bypassing any `React.memo` or `shouldComponentUpdate` checks. Splitting into separate `StateContext` and `DispatchContext` prevents dispatch consumers from re-rendering on state changes.

2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why does React.memo NOT prevent re-renders when a component consumes Context via useContext?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `React.memo` ONLY checks props passed from the parent component! If a component calls `useContext(MyContext)`, React's context dependency propagation directly marks the component's Fiber as dirty when the context value changes, completely bypassing the `React.memo` bailout.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Exposes common misconception about React.memo boundaries.

realWorldUseCases.description: Extracting the useContext call into a small wrapper component so heavy sibling UI components don't re-render.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: function ConsumerWrapper() { const data = useContext(Ctx); return <HeavyChild data={data.specific} />; }

howToExplain.opening: Context updates directly dirty consumer fibers, ignoring React.memo bailouts; selective subscriptions require component extraction or external selector stores.
keyPoints: Decomposing components isolates context consumption to small leaf nodes.
Heavy children receive extracted slices as props and use React.memo.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Decomposing context consumers into small wrapper components is the cleanest native way to tame context re-renders.
analogies: An antenna on a roof: the small antenna receives the radio broadcast and sends a clean wire to the speakers, rather than the entire house vibrating.

commonMistakes.mistake: Wrapping a component that calls useContext in React.memo expecting it to skip context updates.
commonMistakes.why: React.memo only checks props; context subscriptions trigger independent fiber updates.
commonMistakes.correct: Move useContext to a parent and pass the value as a prop to the memoized child.

followUpDeepDive.question: What was the proposed useContextSelector RFC?
followUpDeepDive.answer: A long-standing RFC by Daishi Kato proposed `useContextSelector(Context, state => state.prop)`, which only re-renders when the selected slice changes. This inspired the architecture of Zustand and Jotai.
